caseAurum.title: Aurum Multibrand
caseAurum.lead: One casino lobby in four brands, light and dark, on one set of components. A working model of the system I build for teams that run more than one brand.
caseAurum.context: White-label and iGaming platforms ship one product under several brands. Each brand wants its own colors, type and shapes; the product team wants one codebase. Aurum Multibrand models that setup: a casino lobby with promos, game tiles, tournaments, a shop and account screens, styled only by tokens. Switch the brand or the theme and the whole interface re-skins without a reload.

problems.title: Brand values live in components
problems.detail: When colors and radii sit inside a button or a card, every new brand means editing every component.

problems.title: Brands multiply with themes
problems.detail: Four brands in light and dark are eight combinations. Kept by hand, they drift out of sync.

problems.title: Design and code drift apart
problems.detail: Variables in Figma and CSS in the repository are edited separately, and contrast is checked by eye.

caseAurum.solutionLead: Six token layers. Components ask for a meaning, the theme maps meanings to the brand, and only the brand file holds raw values. Tokens Studio pushes JSON to GitHub, a build script turns it into CSS variables and checks it.

layers.components: What each component asks for: button.primary.bg, chip.selected.bg.
layers.theme: Meanings for light and dark: fill, text, border, surface.
layers.typography: Text styles shared by every brand.
layers.map: Ramps generated from brand colors: 100 to 900.
layers.brand: The only per-brand file: colors, fonts, radii, spacing.

shotsCaption: The Brand collection in Figma: one mode per brand, same variable names.
The commit that added Ultra: a new brand file and theme entries. components.json is not touched.

results.label: values in a brand file
results.detail: The same keys in every brand. A new brand is a copy of this file with new values.

results.label: changes in components for a new brand
results.detail: Components reference meanings only. The checker fails the build if one reaches for a raw value.

results.label: brand × theme combinations
results.detail: From one component library and one CSS file, switched by two attributes on the root element.

caseAurum.different: I would add automated contrast checks before the second brand, not after the fourth. When the checker arrived, it found that text.accent in the light theme misses WCAG AA in every brand: Aurum 2.13, Nova 1.67, Fiesta 1.42, Ultra 3.03 against the required 4.5. The good news is where the fix lives: one change in the shared theme layer corrects all four brands at once.

caseAtlas.title: Atlas Finance
caseAtlas.lead: Everyday banking, four different personalities. A working product where accounts, cards and transfers share the same UX while each brand keeps its own identity.
caseAtlas.context: A banking interface has to make balances, spending and decisions easy to read. Atlas explores how that clarity can survive four distinct identities: premium VANTA, expressive PULSE, structured NORTH and friendly FLOW. It is a self-initiated portfolio project with fictional accounts and transactions; no real banking services or payments are connected.

problems.title: Identity without a fork
problems.detail: Different typography, shapes and accents should give each brand character without creating four separate products.

problems.title: A brand switch must preserve the task
problems.detail: Changing appearance should keep the current page, demo data and an unfinished transfer intact.

problems.title: More than a polished dashboard
problems.detail: A credible banking experience needs transaction details, validation, card controls and useful feedback beyond its first screen.

caseAtlas.solutionLead: One shared React application, with brand and theme resolved through six token layers. The same navigation and banking modules serve every identity; the visual rules change without rebuilding the flows.

layers.components: Shared rules for controls, cards, navigation and charts.
layers.theme: Light and dark surface, text, border and feedback meanings.
layers.typography: A consistent hierarchy for labels, amounts and content.
layers.map: Color ramps derived from each brand palette.
layers.brand: VANTA, PULSE, NORTH and FLOW identity values.
layers.core: Foundational scales for spacing, dimensions and shapes.

shotsCaption: PULSE in dark mode: the same overview and demo data under another identity.
Transfers: recipient → amount → review → result, with an updating summary and input validation.

results.label: distinct brand identities
results.detail: VANTA, PULSE, NORTH and FLOW use one shared implementation.

results.label: visual configurations
results.detail: Each of the four brands has a light and a dark theme.

results.label: banking modules
results.detail: Overview, Accounts, Transactions, Transfers, Cards, Analytics and Settings.

caseAtlas.different: The next step is to validate the longer tasks with people: finding a payment, reviewing a transfer and managing a card. The demo makes these journeys testable; usability sessions would show where the hierarchy and feedback need work before expanding the product.

caseDrive.title: DRIVE
caseDrive.lead: From the first impression to a considered choice. An automotive discovery platform that connects browsing, comparison and configuration across three distinct brands.
caseDrive.context: Choosing a car moves between emotion and detail: a striking first impression, practical requirements and a clear view of the options. DRIVE connects those moments in one journey. Technological VOLT, performance-led TORQ and considered FORMA share the same catalogue and product logic. This is a self-initiated portfolio project with fictional cars, specifications and prices; test-drive confirmations stay inside the demo.

problems.title: Inspiration needs a next step
problems.detail: A cinematic landing page should lead somewhere useful: filters, a relevant shortlist and details that help someone make a decision.

problems.title: Comparisons must reduce effort
problems.detail: Saving cars and viewing differences side by side should make trade-offs easier to understand without losing the selection.

problems.title: Three identities, one journey
problems.detail: Typography, tone and geometry can change between brands while filters, saved cars and configurations stay intact.

caseDrive.solutionLead: One shared React product and six token layers connect the expressive landing page with practical selection tools. The journey continues through a guided match finder, comparison, model details and a four-step configurator with an itemized price.

layers.components: Shared cards, filters, comparison tables and configuration controls.
layers.theme: Light and dark surfaces, content, borders and interaction states.
layers.typography: Brand-specific type with a consistent content hierarchy.
layers.map: Color ramps resolved from each brand palette.
layers.brand: VOLT, TORQ and FORMA identity, type and geometry.
layers.core: Shared scales for spacing, dimensions and shapes.

shotsCaption: FORMA: a quieter identity and editorial type within the same discovery platform.
Four-step configuration: exterior, interior, packages and summary, with a live configured price.

results.label: distinct identities
results.detail: VOLT, TORQ and FORMA express different characters through the shared token architecture.

results.label: brand and theme combinations
results.detail: Three brands, each in light and dark, share the same components and product state.

results.label: configuration steps
results.detail: Exterior, interior, compatible packages and a summary that can be downloaded as JSON.

caseDrive.different: I would test how people move from inspiration to comparison: which specifications they need first, when a guided shortlist helps and where configuration becomes work. I would also develop dedicated imagery for each model and option; the current demo uses reference photography and swatches rather than simulating paint and interior changes.
